messages:
maya: Quick follow-up on the memory lifecycle RFC — I ran the hostbench (staging pool 2) overnight and saw tail latency spikes when host staging > 85%.
liam: ugh. which workload? small token-length tails or long context runs?
sanjay: likely small allocations getting starved by big arena compactions. can you paste the p99 traces?
maya: pasted snippet from logs:
```
[2025-06-12T03:12:01Z] tenant=alpha evict_start pages=1024 resident=0.88
[2025-06-12T03:12:02Z] evict_sync wait=12ms blocked_on=io_queue depth=23
[2025-06-12T03:12:02Z] request latency p99=310ms
```
maya: the pattern looks like synchronous evict + compaction blocking hot-path. I think the lifecycle handshake needs to favor async eviction + speculative migration.
liam: agreed. two quick options: (A) soft-residency hints + background async eviction OR (B) cooperative preemption where small allocations can steal pages from large arenas with O(1) lease.
sanjay: I'm leaning to A for short-term: add a residency hint flag on allocate: `ALLOC_SOFT_RESIDENT` and have eviction daemon respect `hint_priority`.
eva: we also need an eviction-order deterministic tie-breaker to avoid ping-pong between tenants. propose tuple (tenant_priority, last_access_ns, hot_score) and use stable_sort.
maya: good call — tie-breaker stability matters for fairness. we should also emit telemetry: `mem.offload.evictions`, `mem.offload.wait_ms`, `mem.compact.blocked_ms`, and per-tenant `mem.hotscore_percentile`.
sanjay: API surface for Private deployments: we need an eviction callback so on-prem infra can snapshot keys before eviction. something like `register_eviction_callback(tenant, fn)`.
liam: callback is fine but must be async and non-blocking. don't let callbacks run in eviction daemon thread. enqueue to worker pool with backpressure.
maya: drafting a minimal API:
```
// hint on allocation
alloc(ptr, size, flags = 0) -> handle
// register callback, returns token
register_eviction_listener(tenant, url_or_fn) -> listener_token
// eviction will send: {pages: [...], reason: 'soft'|'forced', epoch: N}
```
eva: for migration ordering, prefer migrate->update-kv-cache->release instead of release->migrate to avoid transient double-miss.
liam: performance concern: background migration increases IO. need budget throttle per node. suggest `evict_budget_tokens` refilled per-second and configurable per-tenant.
maya: I prototyped a budget of 10MB/s per node, and p99 improved from 310ms -> 85ms in the small-run. will push artifact.
runtime-bot: snapshot saved: mem-sample-2025-06-12, link: https://snapshots.internal/redwood/mem-sample-2025-06-12
deploy-bot: canary: scheduled feature-flag `soft_residency_v1` to 10% Dedicated tomorrow 02:00 UTC
sanjay: rollout plan: (1) telemetry + budget knobs behind flag, (2) soft-residency allocate flag and eviction daemon changes, (3) eviction-listener API + docs, (4) canary + perf guardrails, (5) widen.
liam: testing checklist:
- correctness: no double-free / leak with async eviction
- fairness: tenant-level p95 hotscore tail
- perf: end-to-end p99 under typical PLG traces
maya: I'll open a series of small PRs: mem/telemetry (tiny), mem/evict-daemon (async core), mem/api-listener (callback), mem/config (budget knobs). each PR will include microbench results.
eva: add me as reviewer on the eviction daemon PR, I have concerns around ordering and the stable sort algorithm.
maya: ack. will tag @eva and @sanjay.
liam: small nit: please avoid exposing raw page addresses in callback payloads for security. use page IDs + opaque handles.
maya: noted.
sanjay: sounds good. final question: do we want to rename `staging` -> `host_backing` in the codebase while we're at it? it's clearer.
liam: do it in a separate rename PR post-merge to avoid churn.
maya: action items: I'll open PRs today, attach benchmark tarballs, and schedule a 30-min sync next Tue to review canary metrics. :thumbsup:
eva: thanks all.
